title: Mark `filter_select()` json as HTML
description:
Fixes #87

This is a small change to mark as HTML the jsonified `options` passed from `filter_select()` to the crosstalk input select widget. Because selectize applies its own HTML escaping, we end up with double-escaped option names, making it impossible to represent characters such as `&` in the options dropdown.

This change is **not applied** to `filter_checkbox()`, because a second round of escaping does't occur client-side.

Here's a minimal reprex:

```r
# library(crosstalk)
pkgload::load_all()

df <- data.frame(
  points = c(10, 12, 14, 21),
  stadium = c(
    "M & T Bank Stadium",
    "Wembley Stadium",
    "FirstBank Stadium",
    "<script>alert('oh-no')</script>"
  )
)

df_crosstalk <- SharedData$new(df)

bscols(
  filter_select(
    id = "stadium_select",
    label = "Stadium Select",
    sharedData = df_crosstalk,
    group = ~`stadium`
  ),
  filter_checkbox(
    id = "stadium_check",
    label = "Stadium Check",
    sharedData = df_crosstalk,
    group = ~`stadium`
  )
)
```

## Before

Before this change, the `&` is rendered as a literal `&` (escaped HTML) and the `<script>` tag is also rendered as double-escaped HTML.

![image](https://github.com/rstudio/crosstalk/assets/5420529/a62debdb-233a-4e8c-98b8-eebd97e1207a)


## After

After this change, the `&` is rendered as HTML `&` and the `<script>` tag appears as literal character strings, and importantly not as a `<script>` tag, showing that selectize is correctly escaping the option labels (and no alert is shown).

![image](https://github.com/rstudio/crosstalk/assets/5420529/bb72bd3d-ddde-41b2-8a6c-2e85313e541c)

title: Update ionrangeslider dependency
description:
Updates ionrangeslider from 2.1.2 to 2.3.1 (by simply copying over ionrangeslider assets from shiny's main branch)

Also makes `filter_slider()` [dynamically themable](https://rstudio.github.io/bslib/articles/custom-components.html#dynamically-themeable-component-1) (as we did in shiny https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/pull/2958), for example:

```r
library(shiny)
library(crosstalk)

ui <- fluidPage(
  theme = bslib::bs_theme(primary = "purple"),
  sliderInput("foo", "bar", 0, 1, 0.5),
  filter_slider("foo2", "bar2", SharedData$new(mtcars), ~mpg)
)

shinyApp(ui, function(...) {})
```

title: Update slider
description:
This PR updates the slider dependency.

I did not update the markup. I took a look at shiny's slider function and, though it seems to differ in a few places, to the best of, my understanding produces the same markup.

The first half of the update script (`tools/updateIonRangeSlider.R` file) is similar to [that of shiny](https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/master/tools/updateIonRangeSlider.R). 
Where it differs:

1. It only uses the [`skinShiny.css`](https://github.com/rstudio/crosstalk/blob/master/inst/lib/ionrangeslider/css/ion.rangeSlider.skinShiny.css) file that already included in crosstalk
2. It imports [shiny.scss](https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/master/inst/www/shared/ionrangeslider/scss/shiny.scss) from shiny to compile Sass -> CSS

@cpsievert let me know if this is the right approach.

title: Another approach to applying default filter/select settings on render
Remove bootstrap
description:
This pull request removes the bootstrap dependency. Bootstrap would often clash when used with rmarkdown, blogdown, or shiny applications that do not import Bootstrap or use a different version than that which is used by crosstalk. 

Bootstrap seems to only be necessary for some minor styling (e.g.: DT with `style="bootstrap"`) and the `bscols` function (bootstrap grid). Removing bootstrap will "break" the former but using flexbox the responsive grid from bootstrap can be closely mimicked.

This thus essentially mainly changes CSS, adding a `crosstalk-row` class, as well as `crosstalk-column-*` (1 through 12) classes. This, however, deprecates the `device` argument of the `bscols`.

description: Travis was failing because npm-shrinkwrap.json has some minor differences between platforms. We actually don't care about differences in npm-shrinkwrap.json, that `git diff --exit-code` line was in there to make sure the generated JavaScript that is committed is up-to-date with respect to the JavaScript source. title: Parameterize min and max in filter_slider
description:
Allows customizing `min` and `max` values. 

For instance, if you want to render from percentage values, none of which hit exact 0 or 100%. A slider from something like 3% to 97% might be not what you want, making it useful to force `min=0` and `max=1`.

Vlad

title: Respect "round" argument in filter_slider
description: This deals with https://github.com/rstudio/crosstalk/issues/41:  the `filter_slider` code was ignoring the `round` argument.  It also changes the documented direction of the value:  `round=1` means nearest 0.1, not nearest 10.  (This is consistent with the `digits` argument of the base `round()` function.)

title: Export the bind() function
description:
As discussed in https://github.com/ramnathv/htmlwidgets/issues/300, the `manipulateWidget::combineWidgets` function sometimes creates `crosstalk` controls after jQuery has called `bind()`, so it is never called for them.  This PR exports bind so that it can be called later for proper initialization.  (`rgl` will call it in the `resize` method, which is called by `combineWidgets` after all components have been created.)

I'm not familiar with Javascript modules, so please check that I did the export properly...

title: Breaking: Simplify selection API
description:
- Remove add/remove/toggle functions from selection module.
  This gives us more flexibility moving forward, particularly the
  option to support multiple key formats at once (Carson has
  proposed more structured key objects) which each plot could
  then choose from based on what formats it knows about.
- Expose FilterHandle constructor directly, to parallel
  SelectionHandle.
- SelectionHandle now uses "this" as the sender property by
  default. It can be overridden using the extraInfo constructor
  param.
- Documentation

title: Add colourpicker library for dynamic changes in selection color palette
description:
Currently I can do "transient" selections like this:

![highlight](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/1365941/17628746/820e8278-607c-11e6-8471-c0dec2e4c0c0.gif)

I would like to enable "persistent" selections, like this, but there is currently no way to alter selection colors to foster comparison:

![eechidna](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/1365941/17628809/bbbc3a2e-607c-11e6-9fbc-404748be5f72.gif)

This pull request takes a step in that direction, with the goal of informing crosstalk about changes in the selection palette (using @daattali's colourpicker library).
